course.title: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
course.instructor: Fei-Fei Li, Ehsan Adeli, with Zane Durante and guest lecturers

figureAudit.note: Counts are for the decks of the covered lectures (lecture 1 has two, lectures 2–7 one each). Lecture 1: eight figure-, chart- and table-heavy slides per deck checked at 600 dpi by an independent reader; part 2 clean, part 1 errors on slides 62 and 64, corrected. Lecture 2: fourteen slides checked; errors on slides 8, 33 and 64 and loose detail on 30, 45 and 63, corrected; eight clean. Lecture 3: nineteen slides checked; errors on slides 80, 84 and 99 and small omissions on 13, 86 and 122, corrected; the absence of optimizer paths on slides 61, 70, 75 and 109 confirmed. Lecture 4: twenty-three slides checked by two readers, who rendered at 150–200 dpi rather than the 600 asked for (crops at 400–600 dpi on slides 11, 53 and 116); errors on slides 11, 25 and 26 and small omissions on 41, 96, 116 and 134, corrected; slide 143's matrices confirmed again on the 1400px render of slide 150; no figure on slide 50 and no optimizer paths on slide 10 confirmed. Lecture 5: twenty-four slides checked by two readers, again at about 200 dpi effective (600 dpi renders downscaled by the viewer), with 600 dpi crops of slides 127, 129 and 133; errors on slides 4, 22, 24 and 81 and small fixes on 35, 38, 80, 108 and 136, corrected; slide 6's matrices, slide 62's K_w x K_h order, slide 101's swapped labels, slide 124's wording, slide 127's numbers and slide 129's minus signs confirmed; slides 81 and 101 checked again on their 1400px renders, which corrected one cell position on 81. Lecture 6: twenty-four slides checked by two readers, who rendered at 600 dpi but read most pages downscaled (about 110–130 dpi), with crops of slides 35, 41 and 73 at 300 dpi and 57, 61, 63 and 65 at 600 dpi; corrections on slides 35 (each VGG stack draws two 3x3 conv, 256 boxes), 41, 63, 73, 75, 78, 79 and 95; slide 11's "per batch" annotation, slide 57's "3x3 conv, 64" label and every histogram value on slides 61, 63 and 65 confirmed; slide 35 checked again on its 1400px render. Lecture 7: twenty-seven slides checked by two readers from crops of 600 dpi renders (eight from page views at about 150 dpi); corrections on slides 7, 58, 61, 88 (the captioning CNN draws 10 conv layers, not 8) and 131; every vector on slides 61–66, slide 67's code listing, slide 111's equation, slide 116's code and slide 129's labels confirmed; slides 65 and 66 checked again on their 1400px renders.

caveats: Covers lectures 1-7 of 18 only; nothing on lectures 8-18.

Lecture 1 has two slide decks, each numbered from 1; cite as 'part 1, slide N' / 'part 2, slide N'. Part 2's printed numbers skip 4, 5 and 45, lecture 2's skip 32 and 49, lecture 3's skip 10, 11, 12 and 29, and lecture 4's skip 2, 47, 112, 113 and 114, so printed numbers run ahead of PDF page numbers. Lecture 5's 141 and lecture 6's 97 printed numbers match their PDF pages. Lecture 7's skip 19, 20, 52, 53, 71, 72, 73, 100 and 103, and its page 118 prints no number (slide 127).
Lecture 1's logistics slides (part 2, slides 33-48 and 50) were not presented in the recording; wiki/course-logistics.md is sourced to the slides as posted on April 1, 2025.

Lecture 2's recording skips its administrative slides (2-4) and ends mid-sentence at 1:06:37, before the multiclass SVM loss (a reading assignment, slides 85-100) and softmax vs. SVM (slides 101-104); those are sourced to the slides alone, and their quiz questions have no printed answers.

Lecture 3's recording skips its administrative slides (2-4) and ends at 1:08:25 in the look ahead to neural networks; slides 100-101 and the appendix of 'Slides from Previous Years' (slides 102-123: Nesterov momentum, AdaGrad, L-BFGS, softmax vs. SVM) are sourced to the slides alone.

Lecture 4's recording skips its administrative slides (3-4) and the 'Today: Deep Learning' examples (slides 12-21: DALL-E 2 and 3, GPT-4, Segment Anything, Sora); those are sourced to the slides alone. It covers the matrix-multiply example (slides 143-150) only in outline.

Lecture 5's recording skips its administrative slides (2-3) and its appendix of 'Slides from Previous Years' (slides 109-141: older convolution and pooling summaries, 1x1 convolutions, the neuron view, the ConvNetJS demo, the deep-learning recipe and a history from the Mark I Perceptron to the Neocognitron); those are sourced to the slides alone. The appendix uses K for the number of filters and F for the filter size, where the lecture uses K for the kernel size.

Lecture 6's recording skips only its course-logistics slide (2), which is sourced to the slide alone; it adds spoken answers on LoRA and on ResNet's paired convolutions (1:04:40-1:06:59) that no slide shows.

Lecture 7's recording skips only its course-logistics slide (2), which is sourced to the slide alone. Several spoken answers go beyond the slides (chunked backpropagation, embedding layers, greedy decoding and beam search); one, on truncated backpropagation through time (31:48-35:36), describes carrying a gradient across chunk boundaries, which the slides do not draw, and the wiki says so. The interpretable-cell colour code (red -1, blue 1) is spoken, not printed.

Lecture 3's optimizer-comparison slides (60, 61's gradient-noise panel, 70, 75, 109) were animations: the PDF shows only the loss surface and legend, so the optimizers' paths are known only from the lecturer's spoken description. Lecture 4's recap slide 10 and lecture 5's recap slide 8 repeat one of these frames.

Lecture 2's deck prints two arithmetic slips in worked examples (slide 60's ship score omits the bias; slide 101's 0.452 is a base-10 log); both are kept as printed and noted. Lecture 3 repeats the slide 101 example as its slide 119, with the same base-10 value, and its slide 34 prints 0.1555 as '15.5%'. Lecture 4's slide 53 prints a plus where a minus belongs in its expanded hinge term, and its matrix-multiply example (slides 143-150) prints an output y that is not the product of its x and w (x times w is [[-1, -1, 2, 6], [5, 2, 11, 7]]); both kept as printed and noted. Lecture 5's deck has four: slide 6 repeats lecture 2's bias-less ship score (61.95 for 60.75), slide 101 swaps its cube labels (the input is 64 x 224 x 224, the output 64 x 112 x 112), slide 124 says 'Conv layer needs 2 hyperparameters' under the heading 'Pooling layer: summary', and slide 129 prints the softmax loss with minus signs in both exponents. Lecture 6's deck has four oddities, none in its arithmetic, each kept as printed and noted: slide 11's LayerNorm annotation says 'Statistics calculated per batch' for N x 1 per-sample statistics; slide 35's VGG16 and VGG19 stacks draw 15 and 17 weight layers (two '3x3 conv, 256' boxes each); slide 57 labels ResNet's last stage '3x3 conv, 64' where slides 53-56 print 512; slides 78-79 point to 'Lecture 13' for visualization, which is lecture 9 in Spring 2025. Lecture 7's deck has six, each kept as printed and noted: slide 65's sampling softmax is wrong in its first two columns (scores (1.0, 2.2, -3.0, 4.1) and (0.5, 0.3, -1.0, 1.2) give about (.04, .13, .00, .84) and (.25, .20, .06, .50), not the printed (.03, .84, .00, .13) and (.25, .20, .50, .05)), which the lecturer acknowledges at 38:42 and 43:21; slide 66's matrix ends rows 2 and 3 in w14; slide 106 writes W_xh and then W_hx; slide 110's chain has a lowercase t where it means T; slide 116's clipping code computes the squared norm and calls it the norm; slide 129 repeats lecture 6's '3x3 conv, 64' label.

Verbatim auto-captions are not published; the transcripts are copy-edits with every restoration listed in their headers, seven passages marked unclear in lecture 1, five in lecture 2, three in lecture 3, one in lecture 4, five in lecture 5, three in lecture 6 and three in lecture 7.
